rows.ARS:
Yellow blend Tea, Cl..
Registration name: Lady Hillingdon, Cl (Tea Cl, Hicks, 1917)
rows.Origin:
Discovered by Elisha J. Hicks (United Kingdom, 1917).
Introduced in Australia by Arthur Yates & Co. Ltd. in 1920 as 'Lady Hillingdon, Cl'.
rows.Bloom: Apricot. Moderate, tea fragrance. Medium to large, semi-double (9-16 petals) bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Climbing. Large, bronze-green foliage.

Height: 12' to 15' (365 to 455cm). Width: 8' to 18' (245 to 550cm).
rows.Parentage: sport of Lady Hillingdon (Tea, Lowe & Shawyer, 1910)
rows.Notes: Dedicated to Alice Marion Harbord (June 23, 1857 Westminster, London - September 13, 1940 Seal, Kent), second daughter of Charles Harbord 5th Baron Suffield, who in 1886 married Charles William Mills (January 26, 1855 - April 6, 1919 Seal, Kent), British banker and politician. In 1898 he became the 2nd Baron Hillingdon.
